answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identities to atmospheric optical telemetry. Nodes authenticate by sampling wavefront fluctuations from a reference nebula observed above a monitored wharf. Because turbulence from a coastal zephyr cannot be simulated, an attacker must deploy discrete optical apertures per identity, incurring substantial hardware costs. However, fog and cloud cover frequently degrade optical line-of-sight, causing verification dropouts.
